## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Mic 4:1-13 is taken as a single reading unit: a universal-pilgrimage hope oracle directly reversing Mic 3:12's devastation (vv1-5), the LORD's regathering of the lame/outcast and restored dominion for "the daughter of Zion" (vv6-8), an abrupt return to present distress and exile to Babylon with a promise of rescue there (vv9-10), and the nations' hostile assembly against Zion turned, unknown to them, into their own judgment, with Zion herself made the LORD's threshing instrument (vv11-13). "Bearing on the inner being" includes: (i) "many peoples"/"many nations," drawn to Zion in pilgrimage (vv1-2) and, later, gathered against it in hostility (v11) — the same collective term spanning two opposite postures; (ii) "we" — Micah speaking for the covenant community's own declared loyalty (v5); (iii) "the lame," "those who have been driven away," "those whom I have afflicted" — the LORD's own regathered outcasts (v6); (iv) "the daughter of Zion," personified, addressed first in coming glory (v8) then in acute present crisis (vv9-10, 13); (v) the LORD, both the source of Zion's affliction (v6) and its healer/redeemer (vv7, 10), and the unrecognised author of the hostile nations' own gathering (v12).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (195/195 non-particle spans). Register shifts markedly within the chapter: elevated future-oracle vision (vv1-5), a further first-person divine oracle of regathering (vv6-8), a jarring shift to direct address in present crisis (vv9-10), narrated hostile intent quoted directly (v11), narrated divine irony (v12), and a closing direct command/declaration (v13).

**Corpus-continuity check.** Immediately-adjacent prior range, found automatically: `Mic 3:1-12` — `iba\app\verse-analysis\Micah\WA-mic-3-debate.md`. Read in full before drafting this debate. Carried forward: "the mountain of the house" (Mic 3:12's climactic verdict — the temple mount reduced to wooded height — directly, almost verbatim reversed at Mic 4:1, "the mountain of the house of the LORD... established as the highest of the mountains"); "the daughter of Zion" (Mic 1:13/3:10's personification, continuing here at vv8, 10, 13); the birth-pain/writhing root (H2342, used at Mic 1:12 for Maroth's own "waiting anxiously," recurring at Mic 4:9-10 for Zion's own labor-pains).

## Per-verse debate

### Mic 4:1

> It shall come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established as the highest of the mountains, and it shall be lifted up above the hills; and peoples shall flow to it,

**Observation.** "It shall come to pass in the latter [H0319] days [H3117G] that the mountain [H2022G] of the house [H1004Q] of the LORD [H3068G] shall be established [H3559H] as the highest [H7218I] of the mountains [H2022G], and it shall be lifted up [H5375G] above [H1931/H9006] the hills [H1389I]; and peoples [H5971A] shall flow [H5102A] to it."

**Operation 1 — the temple mount's own future exaltation, directly reversing its just-declared devastation.**
- **Action-type:** established/exalted (a direct, deliberate future reversal of Mic 3:12's verdict).
- **Subject:** "the mountain of the house of the LORD" — the same site named at Mic 3:12 ("the mountain of the house... a wooded height"), now the subject of its own future exaltation; "peoples," a maximal human collective, drawn to it.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — established as the highest of all mountains, lifted above the hills; a movement — peoples flowing toward it, an image of voluntary, abundant, converging pilgrimage.
- **Source:** unstated grammatically within this verse (passive/stative constructions throughout), continuing the LORD's own declared future acts from the preceding chapters.
- **Target:** n/a directly — the mountain's own exaltation; "it," the destination the peoples flow toward.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Peoples" — a maximal human collective, given a stated future movement (flowing toward the mountain) but no interior motive yet named within this verse (supplied at v2).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as direct future declaration.
- Q4: Source = unstated explicitly within this verse, continuing the LORD's own declared agency from the preceding material.
- Q5: Target = "it" — the mountain, the peoples' own destination.
- Q6: State (exaltation) and movement (flowing).
- Q7: **Major linkage — the chapter's opening reversal.** "The mountain of the house" (H2022G + H1004-root) directly, almost verbatim repeats Mic 3:12's identical phrase for the temple mount, there reduced to "a wooded height," here "established as the highest of the mountains" — one of the clearest, most direct textual reversals in this study's reading of Micah so far, spanning the chapter boundary.
- Q8: "Peoples" — a maximal, undifferentiated human collective, not yet a named nation (contrast v2's "many nations").
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the peoples' own motive for flowing to the mountain is supplied at v2.
- Q11: established/exalted (the mountain); flowed (the peoples).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's opening operation, and its most direct textual reversal of the immediately preceding chapter's climactic verdict.

For out of [H9006] Zion [H6726] shall go forth [H3318G] the law [H8451], and the word [H1697G] of the LORD [H3068G] from Jerusalem [H3389]."

**Operation 1 — the nations' own stated motive: seeking the LORD's instruction, quoted directly.**

- **Subject:** "many nations," now specified (from v1's undifferentiated "peoples"), given directly quoted first-person speech: "Come, let us go up..."; "the God of Jacob," identified as the object of their seeking.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — the nations' own stated desire, quoted directly in their own words, to be taught the LORD's own "ways" and to "walk in his paths" — a genuine, stated interior motive (not inferred), directly echoing the "walk"-vocabulary already used throughout the book (Mic 2:7's "him who walks uprightly," Mic 6:8 anticipated).

- **Target:** the LORD's own instruction ("his ways," "his paths"), sought by the nations.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Many nations" — given the chapter's first directly quoted human speech, a genuine stated interior desire (to be taught), not inferred.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct quotation.
- Q4: Source = the nations' own voluntary desire, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = "his ways," "his paths" — the LORD's own instruction, sought voluntarily.
- Q6: Movement (going up) and state (desiring instruction).
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to v3 (the LORD's own resulting judgment/instruction, enacted); also a genuine tension worth carrying forward against v11 (where "many nations," the SAME term, are later gathered in explicit HOSTILITY against Zion, not pilgrimage) — the same collective label spanning two opposite postures within one chapter.
- Q8: "Many nations" — a maximal collective, given unified, quoted speech ("let us go up").
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: sought-instruction.

**Decision.** Retain — the nations' own stated, voluntary desire for instruction, flagged for direct tension against v11's later hostile assembly of the same collective term.

### Mic 4:3

> He shall judge between many peoples, and shall decide disputes for strong nations far away; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore;

**Observation.** "He shall judge [H8199] between [H0996G] many [H7227A] peoples [H5971A], and shall decide disputes [H3198] for strong [H6099] nations [H1471A] far away [H7350/H5704]; and they shall beat [H3807] their swords [H2719] into plowshares [H0855], and their spears [H2595] into pruning hooks [H4211]; nation [H1471A] shall not [H3808] lift up [H5375R] sword [H2719] against nation [H1471A], neither [H3808] shall they learn [H3925H] war [H4421] anymore [H5750]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own universal arbitration, resulting in total disarmament.**
- **Action-type:** judged/arbitrated (a direct divine act, resolving international conflict); beat-into-plowshares (a stated, voluntary conversion of weapons into agricultural tools, the nations' own resulting act).
- **Subject:** "he" (the LORD, continuing from v2's sought-instruction); "many peoples," "strong nations," "nation... nation" — the same collectives, now recipients of arbitration and, in turn, agents of their own disarmament.
- **Operation:** a movement — divine judgment/arbitration; a movement — the nations' own physical conversion of weapons into tools; a state — the resulting absence of both warfare and the very TRAINING for warfare ("neither shall they learn war anymore" — not merely a ceasefire but an erasure of martial knowledge itself).
- **Source:** the LORD (judgment); the nations themselves (the physical act of beating swords into plowshares, their own response to the judgment).
- **Target:** "many peoples," "strong nations" — recipients of judgment; their own weapons, converted.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Many peoples," "strong nations" — given a stated future condition (disarmament) that is both imposed (by divine judgment) and voluntarily enacted (they themselves beat their own swords).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, direct future declaration.
- Q4: Source of the judgment = the LORD, self, explicit; source of the physical disarmament = the nations themselves, their own act, though enabled/prompted by the prior judgment — Part B.5's distinction directly illustrated.
- Q5: Target = the nations, judged; their weapons, converted.
- Q6: Movement (judgment, conversion) and state (the resulting absence of war/war-training).
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to v13 (a genuine, unresolved tension: there Zion herself is given "horns of iron" and "hoofs of bronze" to "beat in pieces many peoples" — a starkly different, militant image using a DIFFERENT root for "beat" (H1854, not this verse's H3807) — the two visions' relationship is not resolved by this passage's own data, named as an open question below).
- Q8: "Many peoples," "strong nations," "nation... nation" — maximal collectives throughout.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: judged/arbitrated (the LORD); converted-weapons (the nations).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's central peace-vision, flagged for its unresolved tension against v13's later, starkly different image of Zion's own militant threshing of "many peoples."

### Mic 4:6

> In that day, declares the Lord, I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away and those whom I have afflicted;

**Observation.** "In that day [H3117G], declares [H5002] the LORD [H3068G], I will assemble [H0622] the lame [H6760], and gather [H6908] those who have been driven away [H5080], and those whom [H0834A] I have afflicted [H7489A]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own declared regathering of the lame, the driven-away, and those he himself afflicted.**
- **Action-type:** assembled/gathered (a direct, first-person divine act of regathering, explicitly naming three overlapping categories of the vulnerable/scattered).
- **Subject:** the LORD, first person; "the lame," "those who have been driven away," "those whom I have afflicted" — three named categories of Israel's own suffering remnant.
- **Operation:** a movement — active regathering; a striking self-attribution — "those whom I HAVE AFFLICTED," the LORD explicitly claiming responsibility for the very affliction now being reversed, not attributing it to an external cause or the people's own guilt alone.
- **Source:** self — the LORD, explicit, both as the one who afflicted and the one who now gathers.
- **Target:** "the lame," the driven-away, the afflicted — the objects of regathering.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "The lame," "those who have been driven away," "those whom I have afflicted" — three named, vulnerable human categories, given a stated future act (being gathered) rather than a stated interior of their own within this verse.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, first-person divine declaration.
- Q4: Source of the affliction AND the gathering = the LORD, self, explicitly — an unusually direct case of the text attributing both the harm and its reversal to the same single divine agent, without external mediation.
- Q5: Target = the lame/driven-away/afflicted, gathered.
- Q6: Movement throughout.
- Q7: **Forward linkage, shared root.** "Gather" (H6908) recurs at v12 for the LORD's gathering of the HOSTILE nations "as sheaves to the threshing floor" — the identical verb used for two radically different purposes: compassionate regathering of Israel's own outcasts here, and judicial gathering of hostile nations there. Flagged as a significant structural/lexical linkage, not a Q12 instance (both are divine operations, not a human-vs-divine comparison), but a genuine "one verb, two purposes" pattern worth tracking.
- Q8: "The lame," "those driven away," "those afflicted" — collectives defined by shared vulnerability/suffering, not by nationality or locale.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: assembled/gathered.

**Decision.** Retain — a direct divine self-attribution of both affliction and its reversal, and the source of a major "gather" (H6908) linkage carried through to v12.

- Q5: Target = Zion, exiled and redeemed; her enemies, from whom she is redeemed.

- Q7: Direct continuation of v9's labor-pain imagery, now given its specific cause; a further instance of the H2342-root (writhe/labor) already used at Mic 1:12 ("wait anxiously," Maroth) — the same root now applied to Zion's own most acute distress.
- Q8: N/A — addressed as one personified entity.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; this base extract names Babylon explicitly as the place of exile and rescue — taken as this passage's own stated data, without further comment on its relationship to the book's other historical markers (Assyrian-era kings, Mic 1:1).
- Q11: writhed (commanded anguish); exiled (to Babylon); redeemed (there).

**Decision.** Retain — resolving v9's posed question with a specific, named cause and a striking promise of redemption reaching her even in exile itself.

### Mic 4:11

> Now many nations are assembled against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gaze upon Zion.”

**Observation.** "Now [H6258] many [H7227A] nations [H1471A] are assembled [H0622] against [H5921A] you, saying [H0559]: 'Let her be defiled [H2610], and let our eyes [H5869A] gaze [H2372] upon Zion [H6726].'"

**Operation 1 — "many nations," the same collective from v2, now assembled in explicit hostility.**
- **Action-type:** assembled/desired-defilement (a directly quoted, explicit statement of hostile intent — a stark reversal of v2's use of the identical phrase, "many nations," for voluntary pilgrimage).
- **Subject:** "many nations" — the same collective term as v2, now given the opposite posture entirely; their own quoted speech, expressing a desire to see Zion defiled/humiliated.
- **Operation:** a movement — hostile assembly; a state — a directly quoted, explicit desire (not inferred) for Zion's degradation, framed almost as a spectacle ("let our eyes gaze").
- **Source:** self — the nations' own hostile desire, explicit, quoted.
- **Target:** Zion, the object of their desired defilement.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Many nations" — given directly quoted, explicit hostile interior content, the polar opposite of v2's quoted pilgrimage-desire.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct quotation.
- Q4: Source = the nations' own hostile desire, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = Zion, desired to be defiled/gazed upon in humiliation.
- Q6: Movement (assembly) and state (quoted desire).
- Q7: **Major linkage — the chapter's central irony.** "Many nations" (v2, seeking instruction) and "many nations" (v11, seeking Zion's defilement) are the identical term, applied to opposite postures — whether these are the SAME nations at different times, or the term simply recurs generically, is not disambiguated by this base extract; carried forward as an open question, not resolved.
- Q8: "Many nations" — a maximal collective, given unified hostile speech, mirroring v2's unified pilgrimage-speech in form though opposite in content.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; whether vv1-2's pilgrim-nations and v11's hostile-nations are meant as the same party at different points, or as simply the same generic term recurring, is not resolved by this base extract.
- Q11: assembled/desired-defilement.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's central structural irony, "many nations" spanning two opposite postures, flagged as an open question rather than resolved.

### Mic 4:12

> But they do not know the thoughts of the Lord; they do not understand his plan, that he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor.

**Observation.** "But they [H1992] do not [H3808] know [H3045] the thoughts [H4284] of the LORD [H3068G]; they do not [H3808] understand [H0995] his plan [H6098], that [H3588A] he has gathered [H6908] them as [H9004] sheaves [H5995] to the threshing floor [H1637]."

**Operation 1 — the nations' own ignorance, turned into dramatic irony: their hostile gathering is itself the LORD's own gathering, for their judgment.**
- **Action-type:** did-not-know/were-gathered (a stated ignorance, paired with the narrator's own superior knowledge — a classic dramatic-irony construction).
- **Subject:** "they" — the hostile nations of v11, continuing directly; the LORD, the true, unrecognised agent behind their own assembly.
- **Operation:** a state — explicit, stated ignorance of the LORD's own "thoughts" and "plan"; a movement — being gathered (from the nations' OWN perspective, they gathered themselves in hostility, v11; from the narrator's perspective, disclosed here, the LORD has gathered THEM) "as sheaves to the threshing floor" — an image of imminent, total destruction (threshing crushes/separates the grain).
- **Source:** the LORD — explicitly named as the true author of the nations' own assembly, directly subverting their own stated agency at v11.
- **Target:** the nations themselves — unwittingly the objects, not merely the agents, of their own gathering.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The hostile nations — given a stated, explicit ignorance of the true nature of their own situation, a genuine, named interior gap (not knowing/understanding), contrasted directly with the narrator's own disclosed knowledge.
- Q3: Stated explicitly — both their ignorance and the true state of affairs are directly declared, not left implicit.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, explicitly named as the true agent behind what the nations themselves believed was their own initiative (v11) — Part B.5's distinction sharply illustrated: the nations' own stated agency (gathering themselves, v11) versus the deeper, unrecognised divine agency actually at work (gathering them, v12).
- Q5: Target = the nations, unknowingly gathered for their own judgment.
- Q6: State (ignorance) and movement (being gathered/threshed).
- Q7: **Major linkage, shared root.** "Gathered" (H6908) directly repeats v6's identical verb, there used for the LORD's own compassionate regathering of Israel's lame/outcast — the SAME root now applied to the LORD's judicial gathering of hostile nations for threshing. One verb, two purposes, within a single chapter — a significant structural pattern, not a Q12 instance (no human-vs-divine comparison here; both are the LORD's own operations), but a clean example of a single action-type recurring across sharply different divine purposes.
- Q8: "They" — the hostile-nations collective from v11, continuing.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: were-ignorant/were-gathered (unknowingly, for judgment).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's central dramatic irony, and the completion of the H6908 ("gather") linkage begun at v6.

### Mic 4:13

> Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hoofs bronze; you shall beat in pieces many peoples; and shall devote their gain to the Lord, their wealth to the Lord of the whole earth.

**Observation.** "Arise [H6965B] and thresh [H1758], O daughter [H1323G] of Zion [H6726]; for I will make [H7760A] your horn [H7161A] iron [H1270], and I will make [H7760A] your hoofs [H6541] bronze [H5154]; you shall beat in pieces [H1854] many [H7227A] peoples [H5971A]; and shall devote [H2763A] their gain [H1215] to the LORD [H3068G], their wealth [H2428H] to the Lord [H0113] of the whole [H3605] earth [H0776G]."

**Operation 1 — Zion herself, transformed into the LORD's own instrument of threshing against the nations gathered against her.**
- **Action-type:** threshed/crushed (a direct, commanded reversal — Zion, the object of v11's hostile gathering and v12's disclosed divine judgment, now herself the active agent of that judgment's execution).
- **Subject:** "daughter of Zion," commanded and equipped directly by the LORD; "many peoples" — the same term as vv2/11, now the object of Zion's own threshing.
- **Operation:** a movement — commanded threshing, using a striking, powerful-animal metaphor (iron horn, bronze hoofs — imagery of a threshing ox made supernaturally strong); a state/movement — the resulting plunder explicitly "devoted" (a term elsewhere covering total consecration/destruction) to the LORD.
- **Source:** the LORD, explicit — "I will make your horn iron... I will make your hoofs bronze" — Zion's own capacity to act is directly, explicitly sourced to divine empowerment, not self-generated.
- **Target:** "many peoples" — beaten in pieces by Zion's own (LORD-given) strength; their gain/wealth, devoted to the LORD.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Daughter of Zion" — given here her most active, empowered role in the whole chapter (previously afflicted, regathered, in labor-pain, and the object of hostile gathering; now the active agent of judgment).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, direct command and declaration.
- Q4: Source of Zion's own capacity to act = explicitly the LORD's own empowerment ("I will make..."), not self-generated strength — Part B.5's distinction directly and cleanly answered.
- Q5: Target = "many peoples," beaten; their wealth, devoted to the LORD.
- Q6: Movement (threshing) and state/movement (devoting the plunder).
- Q7: **A genuine, unresolved tension, carried forward as an open question rather than smoothed over.** vv1-5 declared universal disarmament ("beat their swords into plowshares... neither shall they learn war anymore," a DIFFERENT root, H3807, for "beat"); v13 now has Zion herself, using a DIFFERENT root (H1854) for "beat," crushing "many peoples" in what reads as active military conquest. This base extract's own data does not resolve how these two visions (universal, voluntary disarmament vs. Zion's own violent triumph) relate — sequential stages, different audiences, or a genuine unresolved tension in the received text — named here as an open question, not settled by outside scholarly harmonisation.
- Q8: "Many peoples" — the same maximal collective from vv2/11, now defeated.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the precise relationship between this verse's militant image and vv1-5's peace-vision is not resolved by this base extract's own data.
- Q11: threshed/crushed (Zion, divinely empowered).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's climactic reversal (Zion from victim to instrument of judgment), with its own real tension against vv1-5's disarmament vision named explicitly as unresolved, not papered over.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **"The mountain of the house" reversed (Mic 3:12 → Mic 4:1)**: the temple mount's devastation, declared at the close of the preceding chapter, is directly, almost verbatim reversed at this chapter's opening — the clearest cross-chapter textual reversal in this study's reading of Micah.
2. **"Many nations" — two opposite postures (vv2, 11)**: the identical collective term used first for voluntary pilgrimage seeking instruction, then for hostile assembly seeking Zion's defilement — whether the same party or a generic recurrence, not resolved by the text itself.
3. **"Gather" (H6908) — one verb, two purposes (vv6, 12)**: compassionate regathering of Israel's own lame/outcast, and judicial gathering of hostile nations for threshing — the same root, radically different divine purposes, within one chapter.
4. **"Strong" (H6099) — nations and remnant (vv3, 7)**: the same descriptor applied first to international powers needing arbitration, then to Israel's own transformed, formerly-lame remnant.
5. **The daughter of Zion's whiplash arc (vv8-10, 13)**: promised restored dominion (v8) → immediate acute crisis, "is there no king in you?" (v9) → named cause and promised rescue, even in exile (v10) → active, empowered agent of judgment (v13) — one of the most emotionally volatile single-figure arcs in the book so far.
6. **The birth-pain root (H2342), cross-chapter**: Mic 1:12 (Maroth's own "waiting anxiously") → Mic 4:9-10 (Zion's own labor-pain at the height of her crisis) — the same root, escalated from a minor town's anxious hope to the mother-city's own most acute anguish.
7. **The unresolved peace-vs-conquest tension (vv3-4 → v13)**: universal, voluntary disarmament (different "beat"-root, H3807) alongside Zion's own commanded, violent threshing of "many peoples" (H1854) — a genuine internal tension in the received chapter, named as open, not harmonised.

## Insufficiencies register

- Whether vv1-2's pilgrim-seeking "many nations" and v11's hostile "many nations" are meant as the same party at different points in a single narrative arc, or as the same generic term simply recurring for different (perhaps unrelated) groups, is not resolved by this base extract's own data.
- The precise relationship between vv1-5's universal, voluntary disarmament and v13's commanded, violent threshing of "many peoples" by Zion herself is not supplied by this base extract — named as an open tension, not harmonised from outside interpretation.
- The specific geographic/historical identity of "tower of the flock" (v8) beyond this base extract's own brief location gloss is not further detailed.
- This passage's own explicit naming of Babylon (v10) as the place of exile, set against the book's Assyrian-era royal dating (Mic 1:1), is not explained or reconciled by this base extract's own data — named here as the text's own stated content, without importing outside historical-critical theory to account for it.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** The "many nations" dual-posture (pilgrimage vs. hostility, vv2/11) is a striking literary device — worth tracking whether this "same term, opposite postures" pattern recurs elsewhere in Micah or the wider corpus as a deliberate rhetorical strategy.
- **EQ2.** The peace-vision/conquest-vision tension (vv3-4 vs. v13) is one of the most significant unresolved interpretive cruxes surfaced in this study's reading of Micah so far — worth returning to explicitly at the whole-book read, and worth comparing against any similar juxtapositions found in later chapters or other prophetic books.
- **EQ3.** The LORD's direct self-attribution of both affliction AND its reversal (v6, "those whom I have afflicted") is a notably candid instance of the text not displacing responsibility for suffering onto a third party — worth comparing against how affliction is sourced elsewhere in this study's reading (e.g., Joel's locust-plague, Jonah's storm).
- **EQ4.** Babylon's explicit naming (v10), while the book's own superscription (Mic 1:1) dates its kings to the Assyrian period, is flagged here purely as the text's own stated content — not a contradiction to be resolved by this instrument, but worth noting for the whole-book read's own synthesis.
